description:
client.rs:254-292 — fetch_session
client.rs:304-345 — call

Both methods read the body via resp.bytes().await then call serde_json::from_slice. serde_json::from_slice accepts UTF-8 input only. RFC 8620 §1.5 states JSON wire format; RFC 7159 §8.1 says JSON text exchanged between systems must be encoded in UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32 (with implementations free to require UTF-8).

This crate effectively requires the server to send UTF-8 JSON. That's the spec-compliant case for any modern JMAP server (RFC 8259 obsoletes RFC 7159 and mandates UTF-8 for network exchange).

The contract gap: a server sending a Content-Type with `charset=utf-8` or `charset=UTF-16` is silently treated as UTF-8 bytes. If the bytes are actually UTF-16, serde_json::from_slice fails with a Parse error that doesn't mention the charset issue. A caller debugging an integration with a non-conformant JMAP server cannot tell from the error why it failed.

Low priority because (a) RFC 8259 makes UTF-8 mandatory, and (b) every shipped JMAP server uses UTF-8. But the doc-comment on fetch_session and call should at least say "Response body MUST be UTF-8-encoded JSON (RFC 8259 §8.1)". Today the contract is just "JSON" without the charset commitment.
title: fetch_session and call do not document body charset handling — what if server sends UTF-16 JSON?
